Bursting with flavor, gourmet vegetarian meal!
Mar 2026 • Solo
"Hum" is an experience, flavors you've never had before, gorgeous presentation and all vegetarian! I started with a hibiscus fig cocktail, paired with a starter of glazed eggplant in holy basil sauce with rice-paper-wrapped seared king oyster mushrooms. Exquisite! Then a pomelo-passionfruit salad, presented in a dainty passionfruit cup. I chose their signature crunchy sticky-rice with Sapa mushrooms main dish, which was accompanied by lightly pickled ginger & lemongrass, and kumquats. So satisfying! And for dessert jujube jam rolls with tart homemade key-lime ice cream and fresh, sugar-glazed tamarind.... this is seriously my new favorite dessert! Such a delight.

Wonderful
Dec 2025 • Couples
I am vegetarian. We had had the a la carte in the other restaurant (which also does meat dishes) and loved it so much we wanted to try the signature menu. We absolutely loved it. We were looked after by the excellent and very charming Hang Nguyen. She explained all the dishes to us and was very knowledgeable . We also had a nice encounter with the customer care manager who checked we were happy with everything. About the food: Each dish showcased the different vegetables beautifully. The flavours were very subtle and with our British palate I would say you have to eat slowly and consciously to appreciate the flavours and the details that have gone into each dish. I would describe the whole meal as light, but sufficient, and we appreciated this as there is nothing worse than feeling utterlly stuffed; I didn't wake up hungry. It is expensive, but only relative to Vietnamese prices and certainly still cheap vs. the UK, and think it is a fair price for the ingredients that have been very carefully sourced, the quality of the dishes and the whole experience. We would most definitely return if we had the opportunity.

Style over substance
Nov 2025 • Couples
Hum signature is a tasting menu, which highlights a number of vegetables we’d not really come across. Each dish is presented with detailed background to the ingredients by an enthusiastic waiting team. 

Whilst the design of the meals is impressive and there are a number of courses - we were still hungry at the end. The first three courses are served together and are thimble sized. For the price, this is not good value for money and as a result we would not recommend. It would not be hard to increase the quantity that was on offer. Some dishes, especially the last dish (I think white lotus) were completely bland. 10 out of 10 for effort but more style over substance. The main Hum restaurant is excellent and offers much better value for money. The ambience in the latter is also nicer.

Hum Signature - a future michelin restaurant?
Mar 2025 • Couples
We booked Hum Signature for our first night in Vietnam and it was an evening of delight and culture. The building itself is eclectic, fascinating and requires a guide to get you to the right place. The atmosphere was refined, welcoming and hinting at something special to come. They certainly didn't disappoint, each dish was perfectly crafted to provide a visual feast almost too good to eat. However, you'll certainly not regret taking any bite of each dish, each mouthful was filled with different textures and flavours and we challenge anyone to notice there was no meat in any of the dishes. We had the tasting menu, which ensured a continued stream of delightful dishes. The taste, balance and volume of each dish was perfectly managed to ensure that you were satisfied at the end of the meal. 

I understand that the tasting menu was relatively new when we visited and Michelin should certainly put it on their list to visit this year.

Dear Alex K ,
Thank you for visiting Hum Vegetarian and taking your time to write to us. We are glad to clarify with you the VAT and Service charge at Hum. Value Added Tax (VAT), also called “Good and Services tax” or “Consumptions tax” in other countries, is the indirect tax that the end-users pay for their products. According to Vietnam's law, the rate of 10% is compulsory for an officially registered company with its tax payment responsibility, such amount collectable by our Tax Authority. Regarding service charge, it contributes to the staff income and is a common fee in the hospitality industry as a sign of recognition of the staff quality service. By indicating both the VAT and the service charge on every page of our menu, we are confident of having exercised clear communication of all charges to all visitors. We value your opinion on this. Luxury (translated: expensive - for Vietnamese) place for foreigners. Why? Because we are searching on TripAdvisor for advices. The winner-takes-all. You search for the top 10 vegetarian restaurants on Google and this pop up with the highest score then you choose it and forgot the rest.

First, let's dive a little deep about the services:

1- There was no problem with the booking process through the phone, the staff was friendly and professional. I didn't have a chance to ask for her name.

2- Unfortunately, they brought me dishes and drinks that I didn't order, for 2 times. 

Over all, it's okay about the services.

Second, Food (on the Vo Van Tan street)

1- It's not the traditional Vietnamese vegetarian. It's a combined flavors Western vegetarian in a luxury Eastern-style restaurant that suits well with foreigners. That's why there are too many positive reviews from foreigners about this restaurant.

2- In my opinion, the Canh Chua Nha Hum (Sour soup a la hum) is a MUST TRY. A hot (but didn't last long), spicy and sour soup. It's not the traditional Vietnamese Canh Chua. It tastes like a fine combination of the spicy of Tom Yum and the sour of the Vietnamese Canh Chua. More like a vegetarian Tom Yum than Canh Chua.

If you want to eat something like the old traditional Vietnamese, try: Rau Que Kho Quet (Veggies with "kho quet") . Kho Quet (Mam Kho Quet) is a sauce to eat with vegetables. 

3- Drinks. 

I tried the Orange, Carrot and Ginger. They said it's healthy, maybe from the inside because my brain said the different. 

Over all: 

It's good to try something new. But I'm a Vietnamese, I prefer the traditional vegetarian. There are many restaurants in HCMC but you won't find it on TripAdvisor or any popular apps for foreigners because they got dominated by all the high scores restaurants. Try Foody app for the local restaurants.

A very kind gentleman, Phuong, referred to himself as the "guest manager," and he was very hospitable and helpful, checking in with us to make sure that everything was satisfactory, ordering a taxi for us at the end of our meal, getting me the recipe for a delicious cocktail, offering us a tour of the restaurant, etc. That cocktail, by the way, was a hazelnut caipiroska, a drink that I know I'll be making back at home.

If Hum were in our home town, we would definitely be regular customers. Whether or not you are vegetarian, I highly recommend that you plan to enjoy a meal at Hum!

Before anything, I would like to say that I am a carnivorous (can’t live without my meat) and it was really a challenge for my friend to make me try a pure vegetarian restaurant.
First of all, you need to open your eyes to manage to find Hum! You can easily pass in front of it without noticing it.But once you spotted it, it’s like finding a real treasure!
The decor is beautiful thanks to the choice of colors, furniture and old-fashioned tiles. Passed the mysterious entrance corridor, you reach a tranquil haven of lush greenery.
I was first enchanted by the atmosphere and decoration, sophisticated but so simple at the same time that you immediately feel comfortable. The table set-up is exquisite and I loved the chopstick presentation cover made of banana leaf. Once you are presented the quite extensive menu, you realize that a few items could be worth trying.
But the real surprise came along with the food itself. First you are blown away by the dish presentation looking mouthwatering, then by the incredible taste!! Yes, I am shamelessly writing that vegetable can have taste! Emphasis seems to be put on getting the perfect match of vegetable taste and texture with fantastic sauces. Each dish is accompanied by an explanation of which healthy benefits it will bring to your body (which is also appreciated as everybody says that veg are good for health…but what for exactly?!).
The staff is also very friendly and professional. When I couldn’t stop expressing the pleasure I was having with all these delicious dishes, the waiter offered to call the chef (Diep) to come and say hi.
I was not very fond of the fried rice à la Hum (a bit too dry for my liking, next time I will try another one) and the black glutinous rice yoghurt (the black rice is fermented and I’m not fan of this taste at all), but I seriously recommend the following: deep fried à la Hum tofu, steamed mushrooms in coconut, king oyster mushrooms with green apple sauce and as dessert, toddy palm in coconut milk.Delicious!!
Obviously with such an extensive selection I was expecting a high bill, but guess what: 44$ for all of that (except that I was offered the toddy palm as I did not eat the black rice yoghurt, thank you very much to Hien Bui, the assistant operations manager) including also a passion martini and a bottle of sparkling water! Truly amazing experience.
The 3 sine qua non conditions for a stunning restaurant are here gathered at Hum: decor, service and food.This restaurant is a sheer success and is really worth visiting!
Keep up the good work and see you next year!

The jicama and tofu was really flavorful, though there were only 3 pieces of tofu and I really wanted more.

Even the "mild" dish seemed pretty spicy, so keep that in mind when you tell them your taste. 

The staff is very friendly, there is free wifi, and the menu is in English & Vietnamese. They have drink specials for happy hour (before 6pm, I think). The restaurant is open all day from 10am-10pm.

All said and done we paid about $30 USD for 2 mains, 1 appetite, 1 glass of wine, 1 juice and 2 waters. A little pricey by HCMC standards but totally reasonable given the quality.

Also good are the pad thai noodles or lotus seeds and steamed rice served in a half a pineapple.

My favorite salad is their Rainbow Salad; fresh raw veggies grated and dressed with lemon sesame dressing. 

Drinks here are also pretty wonderful. My fiends seem to like the kumquat pink tea, which is a sweet concoction of kumquat and sugar water over ice. I like it too, but if I'm not so much into sweet that day, I'll go for their fresh lemon grass/ ginger tea, either hot or over ice.

Sep 2015 • Business
Hum was a refreshing find for our group in fast-paced HCMC. It was our first meal in the city and we could not have had a better introduction to vegetarian Vietnamese food. Naturally for non-vegetarians like us, we were intrigued about vegetarian Vietnamese cuisine which is famous for its beef pho and seafood spring rolls. The meal was a complete revelation to what Vietnamese food can be. It was beautifully presented, backed up by charming, efficient service.
All the dishes we ordered hit the mark and then some. The fried tofu was great, as were the pineapple fried rice and stewed egg in claypot. The stir-fried green beans were crunchy and fresh.
The location could not be better. Situated in a cute old house just next to the War Remnants Museum, it had a small attractive fish pond and shady trees along the walls. 
The service, as stated, was exceptional. All the staff spoke pretty good English and came with a smile at lunchtime. The manager dropped by to ensure everything was okay.
Ho Chi Minh City is wonderful for street food and more traditional fare, but if tere is one meal you would want to be different and an eye-opener, Hum would be a good choice.

Don't doubt the vegetarian brilliance!
Aug 2015 • Couples
Hum was one of the most fascinating and interesting of our food experiences in Vietnam. 

Firstly, it's set in a beautiful restaurant that is Balinese style with large Buddhas, little ponds and bridges, and lovely decor. 

Secondly and most importantly, the food is really something special. 

Neither of us are vegetarians and I personally hesitate to eat anywhere vegetarian but I'd read such great things that I had to try it out. 

So, the menu is expansive. 

You won't go hungry and you'll definitely find something that will make you salivate or interest you enough to order. Most dishes have great English descriptions as well as the reasons why the ingredients are good for you e.g. "promotes healthy blood flow", "good for weight loss" etc. We had a great time ordering an array of dishes and really enjoying them. 

We had a lovely thick gingko soup that was really flavoursome. The deep fried vegetables are a must as they deep friend everything including large Thai basil leaves with a great dipping sauce and we loved the dish. The spring rolls are executed with artistic perfection, packed with ingredients in a whirl of colours. Our favourite was the mushroom coconut curry served in a coconut. This was such a different curry, tasting like red curry but a bit milder with succulent large juicy strings of mushroom. A dish worth coming back for! 

They also have lovely juices and currently offer a buy 2 get one free so dining as two we were treated to three and loved them all - all natural and all well balanced. 

The staff are attentive and friendly and the location about 50m down from the War Remnants museum makes this is a must stop food experience for anyone discovering the fabulous food of Ho Chi Minh City. Plan to do this place and the museum together and you'll have a great HCM outing! Bon appetite!

My cocktail arrived, "excuse me sir! your cocktail please enjoy it", "can you just put it down please". This sets the tone for the service, everything is an interruption, an event. Before the food arrives the waiter comes by "excuse me, excuse me" (we are in the middle of a conversation) he asks if we are sharing a meal or eating separately. We answer sharing. This turns out to be code for is it ok if one of your plates comes out 20 minutes before the other. This is just plain bad. Its this clumsiness that permeates the whole experience. Down to simple details; they wrap the chopsticks in some kind of leaf. Its a nice touch. But your robbed of the chance to enjoy this because when your plates arrive the waiter takes your chopsticks aside to unwrap them, why? The food arrives with what is by now the usual disruptive fanfare (one plate at a time). We are eating, as I mentioned earlier its excellent. Four people turn up, "excuse me, excuse sir can you move" and this is where things go from clumsy to terrible. You do not move people when you have already served food (unless at their request) you just don't. We refuse. 
Some people reading this may say, 'but your in Vietnam'. And I agree a certain tolerance for language barriers etc goes a long way. But I don't believe in the mindset 'good for Vietnam' – not at this level and I'm sure management don't just want to be a good restaurant 'in vietnam', but good anywhere. This could be a great restaurant, but the service has a long way to go.

Mouse in restaurant
Jun 2015 • Couples
This is my first tripadvisor review but I really feel that I had to share our experience. My husband and I had eaten here a couple of days ago and were so impressed that my husband, an avid meat eater, suggested that we return here for our last night in Vietnam. We have just returned from the restaurant and we are both utterly disgusted. We were coming towards the end of our very enjoyable meal when I saw a mouse drop from the corner of the roof onto a shelf and run the full length of the restaurant along the top shelf of a unit along the wall in the main dining area. I pointed it out to my husband and the staff in the area saw it but did nothing. The manager passed by a few seconds later and asked how the meal was. I told him about the mouse and was very surprised at the reply which was that it was only a small mouse and they are very hard to catch. We immediately asked for the bill, which to my utter disbelief contained a service charge. I called the waiter who had been serving us and explained that we did not want to pay the service charge (to be honest I was tempted to refuse to pay the bill but resisted the urge). He called the manager who came over and explained that this is a normal fixed charge that the company applies. I replied that because of the mouse and the response, we were not happy to pay the service charge (approx €3 but still a huge nerve to ask for it under the circumstances). He again apologised and said he would get the cashier to remove it from the bill. Another waitress returned with the amended bill with just the service charge removed and apologised about the mouse, her excuse being that the restaurant is set in a garden, true but not a reasonable excuse to have vermin in the dining area. As we were leaving I told the manager that if this was a restaurant at home that the entire meal would have been free of charge and that he should consider that the next time it happened. Utter disgust and disappointment.

Elegance and tranquility
Nov 2014 • Business
Saigon is an incredible city, full of life, noise and humidity. If you want to escape the chaos for a couple of hours and at the same time enjoy some of the best vegetarian food you will ever eat, then this is the place to come.
We had fresh spring rolls as well as fried spring rolls to start with and both were divine. You can't even count all the flavours as they explode in your mouth. Each dish comes with its own accompanying side of sauce, which obviously complement the dish and give you an extra little kick of spice and flavour.
We then went on to have bean salad, spinach rice and steamed mushroom in a coconut shell. Absolutely incredible flavours, textures, presentation, service, we were completely blown away. 
We also tried a couple of juice cocktails, which had the same fresh, healthy and relaxing feel. The service is excellent and the ambience cool and calming in the middle of a chaotic and steamy city.
We spent about $32 which is expensive for here but really reasonable compared to the UK and there was a lot of food for this amount.
Just be aware that they don't actually accept US dollars, you'll need Vietnamese Dong but there is an ATM right outside.

I was very excited to visit Hum due to the overwhelming amount of positive feedbacks about this so call "innovative" and "unique" vegetarian fine dining restaurant. However, most of my expectations were not met. Hum is beautiful, and that really is the only positive thing I can say of it. Even though I am a resident of Ho Chi Minh City, Hum reminds me of my dining as a tourist. I found out about the restaurant through ranking list and reviews on websites like tripadvisor. And when I got to the restaurant, it is often disappointing. If I was a tourist visiting HCMC, Hum would definitely get on my radar, however, as a residential foody, I would not choose to visit Hum again. 

Food: Hum has a small menu. I have been to many vegetarian restaurants, and the food at Hum is only average. There are nothing "innovative" or "unique" about the menu. I have had most of the dishes at Hum done better somewhere else. Some of the food brought to my table was even cold. Hot pots are not recommended.

Price: Really expensive even for a normal portion (shared among 3-4 people) let alone Hum serves minuscule portion. Most of the dishes range above 75,000 VND compared to 50,000 - 60,000 VND at other fine vegetarian restaurants. Drinks are also absurdly expensive, 80,000 VND for a pot of tea. In addition, I got shortchanged 100,000 VND and only caught that mistake when I asked to see the bill when I got my change (the bill was not given to me after I paid). 

Service: staffs are cold. However, I did arrived on one of the busiest night. Hum has enough staffs to answer to your needs quickly. Nonetheless, I rarely saw a smile, and most of them seem very aloof. 

Atmosphere: great. I like the background music, the decoration, and the seating.
 
Tips:

- Make reservation. Despite my unfulfilling experience, this is a popular restaurant so it is best to preserve your place before coming.
- Downstair is the most beautful. Second flr is smaller, and third floor is hot. 
- Be careful when you pay and ask to keep the receipt afterward. 
- Food is generally spicy. So if you can't handle too much heat, ask the staff to bring it down a notch. They are pretty understanding of that. 
- Hot pots are so not recommended. 
- I do have recommendations for decent Vietnamese style vegetarian food (Hum is Thai oriented) so pm me if you're interested.

Having read the rave reviews for this restaurant, I have wanted to dine here since landing (2 weeks ago), but because I am the only vegetarian in my group, I waited till I had a night free to myself. I finally had that chance earlier this evening, and I am sad to say my experience fell far short of my expectations. Granted, the garden, building and general ambiance was just as nice as so many reviewers have noted. So if you dine for those reasons alone, you'll be happy dining at ...hum. However, in my case, the hope of soaking in some of that "Zen-like" vibe was soon dashed after the staff relegated me to the attic: a stuffy, windowless and dimly lit room with no recognizable decor. Plain is one thing, uninspired is another. As a lonely solo diner, I felt even lonelier in the attic, with nothing to look at but the wall and a blank table: no napkins, no water, nothing. The waiter was pleasant enough and helped me a bit with the menu, but from there on out it was a steady slide downward; the five stars that I thought I'd surly give ...hum began to flicker and die out. The passion(fruit) smoothie I had ordered well before I had ordered any dishes came to my table well after I had finished eating the main dish, green curry. I felt was an ordinary green curry mild enough for an infant. I have had many green curries in my life, and while ...hum's curry is not offensive, it is run of the mill with the flavor profile of Gerber baby food. By contrast, the smoothie was actually very tasty. Only after finishing the smoothie did the deep-fried square "spring rolls" arrive... the appetizers I had naturally assumed would come after the smoothie, but before the main dish! After all this jumbling of things, I'm surprised I didn't get the bill before eating my meal! The squares were interesting, but nothing out of this world. The dipping sauce they came with tasted as if it were straight out of a bottle. Neither the waiter nor any other person asked me how I found the food, nor if I needed anything else (e.g., a glass of ice water or tea), something that is standard at even the humblest street-side lunch cafes serving 20,000 VND lunches! At best, ...hum is a beautiful establishment that may possibly offer finer dishes than the ones I ordered. Also, the prices are quite reasonable, though a bit smallish. At worst, ...hum is over-rated (There's no way it deserves the #2 spot in a city filled with excellent eateries). 

...hum? I say, "ho-hum." I am hoping my 2 stars will cool the hype a bit, and allow for more deserving eating establishments in HCMC to shine a bit brighter. 

Finally, please note that this review was written by a person who has been vegetarian for over 25 years, and is on his 4th visit to HCMC. Hope that that affords me a bit of credibility. Thank you.

Fantastic flavorful food!
Dec 2016 • Couples
Somehow the setting manages to be peaceful despite its central location...

I am vegetarian but my boyfriend is not and we were both very satisfied with the meal. The menu is, quite frankly, overwhelming - there are so many options and they all sound great and as someone who is used to picking between 1-3 vegetarian options, this is a delightful problem. It's predominantly Vietnamese with a few Thai and Western dishes.

We went with fresh spring rolls, which looked gorgeous and were crisp and refreshing. The white curry was something we had never seen before - somewhere between a curry and a tom ka, with lots of mushrooms and rice vermicelli on the side. The jicama and tofu was really flavorful, though there were only 3 pieces of tofu and I really wanted more.

Even the "mild" dish seemed pretty spicy, so keep that in mind when you tell them your taste. 

The staff is very friendly, there is free wifi, and the menu is in English & Vietnamese. They have drink specials for happy hour (before 6pm, I think). The restaurant is open all day from 10am-10pm.

All said and done we paid about $30 USD for 2 mains, 1 appetite, 1 glass of wine, 1 juice and 2 waters. A little pricey by HCMC standards but totally reasonable given the quality.
